conceptZh: 葉：樹上長出的葉子；太空人玩偶和一陣風把落葉拉成字。
object: a bouncy astronaut toy in a fishbowl helmet and a gust of wind pulling cartoon leaves in opposite directions
morph: tug-of-war over a floating leaf-vine between the astronaut and a puff of wind, until the leaf pieces spring together into 葉
creativeAngle: 太空人玩偶在不對的時機飄離地面，和一陣風玩拔河，拉著葉子兩端，最後啪地彈回原位拼成葉字。
promptEn: An 8-second bright, clean toy-animation clip on a solid pale sky-blue backdrop. Cast: one bouncy astronaut toy in a round fishbowl helmet, with a stubby orange suit and a stubby antenna, who keeps floating off the ground at the worst moment, and one cartoon puff of wind with a cheeky face. The only text on screen is the single Traditional Chinese glyph 葉, drawn in saturated forest-green strokes, ending centered, uncropped, about 70 percent of frame height with margins. 0.0-1.5s: the astronaut bounces in, grabs the end of a long green leaf-vine, and with a jolly hop drifts upward with his boots dangling, still holding on. The first narrated 葉 lands as a broad green leaf shape floats down into frame. 1.5-3.5s: the wind puff blows in from the right and grabs the other end of the vine; tug-of-war begins, the leaf stretches like taffy, the astronaut skids sideways in mid-air and spins, and the leaf pieces slide apart into the separate parts of the glyph. The second narrated 葉 lands as the stretched pieces spring back together with a bouncy boing and click into the correct strokes of 葉. 3.5-5.0s: the wind gives one big happy puff, the astronaut lets go, floats up in slow motion with startled round eyes, then bumps gently against an invisible ceiling and plops back down. As the word 樹葉 is spoken, a little cartoon tree sprouts at the edge of the frame and shakes a few extra green leaves down around the astronaut's shoulders. 5.0-8.0s: the glyph is perfectly still and clear for the last 3 seconds while the astronaut, standing beside it, balances a single leaf on his helmet like a hat and does a small happy bounce, and the wind puff gives a tiny wave. Audio: a warm, friendly off-screen voice speaks slowly and distinctly in clear Taiwanese Mandarin with clear tones and no erhua, reading exactly these syllables: 葉、葉、樹葉 (ㄧㄝˋ、ㄧㄝˋ、ㄕㄨˋ ㄧㄝˋ). The character twice with a short pause, then the word once, then stop. The word is audio only. No background music, no extra speech, no subtitles or flashing effects; stylized toy and cartoon characters only, no real people.
